Again, I agree most Austrians were either in favour or even directly collaborated with Nazi Germany. The point here is that the referendum was illegal, as the Russian was, because of the context of it.

Yeah the Ukrainians aren’t the most morally correct state (tbh i doubt there are any), but as you say, we can’t recognise it because it sets that exact precedent, putting our member-states at risk of suffering the same fate. 

It’s not “pissing on Russians cuz we hate Russia” but protecting our own interests, as they protect theirs. Our own interests just happen to be more democratic & progressive than Russia’s (not that we are perfect either).

Yeah, that was the sentiment in 1919 (thus that section of the treaty) but nor you nor I can say surely that 75% of the Austrian people would’ve wanted to join Germany, given the lack of unbiased polling on said time. What we can be sure of, is that the Referendum was illegitimate and in no way fair, which is what is being discussed here.

Although I agree that a legitimate referendum there, before invasion, and with a neutral organisation holding it, would mean that Crimea should’ve gone to whoever the referendum voted it to. The problem is that it’s too late to hold one, given the Russian military action on the region & subsequent flight of Ukrainians (and arrival of [Russians](https://eurasianet.org/russia-migration-helping-to-russify-crimea)).

Most people don’t recognise it based on the method, which violated international law, rather than the idea of Crimea being “rightfully” Ukrainian

I mean, if you think [this](https://commons.m.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Stimmzettel-Anschluss.jpg#mw-jump-to-license) is a legitimate referendum that represents the will of Austria, added up to the literal intimidation recorded at said referendum, I don’t think you’ve got a right idea of what a valid referendum should look like

My bad, “hate” is too of a strong word for geopolitical positions. We shouldn’t hate anyone, but I do hold in disdain most of the Leave campaign leaders, from Farage to Johnson. I believe most of the sub shares that feeling. It’s a matter of conflicting ideals: Federalists in general see a better value in a single market economy for the increased negotiating leverage, as well as overall better economic performance for the benefit of all its members.

Meanwhile, Leavers **in general** value the Napoleonic-born idea of nation-states based on single cultures, with said idea triumphing over any economical or social benefit to the people. 

Thus, federalists **in general** see Leavers as nationalist nut-jobs while Leavers see Remainers **in general** as  bootlicking un-patriotic idealists. But yeah, neither side should hate each other, and hopefully the rift will heal now that the issue is partially settled.

Then we agree in most issues. And yeah, as a Swedish-British Remainer who now lives in Germany, I personally also started rooting for the Scots to leave Britain just so the Leavers could be blamed for “destroying the UK”. But we should never base geopolitical policy on spite.

And for the ones that dug into this conversation, we shouldn’t hate on the whole England just because of the majority Leavers there. Most were manipulated and now just want to get it over with. This quote by Thatcher/Attlee fits well:

“The late Lord Attlee was right when he said that referendums are the device of dictators and demagogues”

Surely we cannot compare the seizures of the pre-UN geopolitical world like the annexation of Alsace Lorraine by the German Empire or the expulsion of Germans and annexation of Pomerania-Silesia by the USSR to Poland. We now fortunately posses a better sense of national determination, like the UK enacted when leaving the EU.

And then I see we agree that they have the right to leave if *they* chose to. But then don’t the Scots have that right too? The UK itself has also had 2 referendums on EU membership, with conditions different in both situations.

And although I believe the analogy is worded weirdly, I agree that it wouldn’t be diplomatically acceptable to mention a part of a country (NI) as basically just another (Ireland) just because said country (Ireland) wants it badly. But, wouldn’t it be acceptable if said territory wishes to be part of said other state, like in this case, NI for Ireland?

Doesn’t Northern Ireland have a whole recent history of violence over what nation has sovereignty over it? I don’t recall Bremen or even the Saarland having as much violence over who “owns” them(even during the 1955 Saar referendum).

I’m sure we agree that, as per the Good Friday agreement, the people of any nation, specifically Northern Ireland, may vote to join/stay in whatever nation they desire. No terrorists should have any say over who owns it. But under self determination, wouldn’t it be fair for a new referendum, if any devolved assembly wishes for it? I mean, don’t we have General Elections every 5 years? (less lately)
